Outcome_variable.evidence_source: [/page/9/Text/11] Regarding the relationship between the sense of identity and LS, in both variable-centered and person-centered approaches the results were almost the same for Japanese and US adolescents. These results suggest that the relationship between identity type and LS may be the same across cultures.

sample_type.evidence_source: [/page/9/Text/11] The results obtained from Japanese youth revealed the universality and uniqueness of identity development. [/page/10/Text/3] Specifically, in early and middle adolescence, Japanese adolescents have clear goals for the future, and they know what they need to do to achieve them (e.g., academic achievement), and this choice is accompanied by the generous support of parents and teachers (Stevenson & Zusho, 2002). In contrast, after graduating from high school, late adolescents and young adults have to prepare to enter society and, thus, face identity issues in earnest (Sugimura & Mizokami, 2012). Japanese youth in these stages are not clear on what to do and tend to be confused.
